answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can price identity in work, not fees. Picture arrivals at a wharf: each new agent must pass a challenge graded by a standing jury before it earns anything, so forging identities costs real effort per pseudonym. Peer attestations then act like a prism, splitting each agent's behavior into a public track record — and a violet flag on planted junk slashes the grader, making fake vouching more expensive than honest work.
